title: Payment serialization declares validation order and mutation on failure
question: Compare entry-point guards, shared validators, normalization, partial object mutation and assertion evidence.

evidence.title: Serialization entry points do not share the same rejection boundary
explanation: Basic direct debit validates parties before building XML, but transfer output calls no required-field validator; XML functions mutate stored identifiers and missing IDs are filled from time. Validation and formatting are observable steps with different preconditions.

The two supplied PHPUnit-named examples only write XML files and contain no assertions. They do not prove validation, nonmutation, determinism, totals or output correctness. Error paths may occur after format/ID/party mutation; no in-memory rollback is implemented.

evidence.title: Currency decoder failures can mutate destination and nullable validity
explanation: Currency decoders assign failed parse results before reporting error, while nullable wrappers change Valid before delegating.

ParseCurr returns XXX on invalid code. UnmarshalJSON/Text and supported Scan types assign that result then wrap error; unsupported Scan types skip currency assignment. NullCurrency sets Valid=true before nonnull delegation, so an unsupported type can preserve old currency with changed Valid. JSON currency decoding strips quotes without JSON-unescaping, rejecting escaped valid codes. These are actual currency decoder state boundaries, not automatically Core Money failure atomicity.

Decode invalid supported text into a populated Currency or decode unsupported nonnull value into an invalid NullCurrency; escaped JSON code exposes lexical issue. Exactnull resets nullable state and is a no-op for plain Currency JSON. No Currency decoder execution or enclosing Money-operation mutation was observed. Static review of the pinned bodies and prior attributed dependency contracts only; no upstream build, runtime outcome, deployed state or concurrency schedule was executed.
